name: Caste Certificate
description: Comprehensive guide to applying for SC, ST, and OBC caste certificates in India with verified lineage rules, cut-off dates, and portal steps.

national.title: How to Apply for Caste Certificate in India (2026)
national.summary: Master procedure for obtaining an official Caste Certificate for SC, ST, and OBC categories under Indian constitutional orders. Verified guide covering paternal genealogy proof, pre-cutoff residence records, Talati verification, and digital certificate download.

steps.title: Trace Paternal Bloodline and Caste Proofs
steps.description: Collect caste proofs of your father, grandfather, or paternal uncle. Under Indian law, caste status is inherited strictly through the paternal lineage.
steps.where: Family Archives or District Records Office
steps.calloutText: Caste proofs of mother or maternal relatives are not legally admissible to claim caste status.

steps.title: Establish Ancestral Residence Before Statutory Cut-Off Date
steps.description: Gather ancestral revenue records showing family residence before 1950 for SC and ST, or before 1978 for OBC. Suitable proofs include old land records, birth registers, or school admission registers.
steps.where: District Record Room or Taluka Archive
steps.calloutText: Cut-off years establish that your family resided in the state when constitutional caste orders were first notified.

steps.title: Draft Family Genealogy Tree and Caste Affidavit
steps.description: Prepare a family genealogy chart showing relationships from the eldest known paternal ancestor to the applicant. Execute a sworn caste affidavit on non-judicial stamp paper before a Notary Public.
steps.where: Notary Office or District Court Complex
steps.calloutText: The family tree must clearly list male ancestors in direct lineage with their birthplaces.

steps.title: Obtain Local Talati or Patwari Attestation
steps.description: Submit your family tree and caste proofs to your village Talati or ward revenue inspector. The officer verifies local community recognition and signs the inquiry report.
steps.where: Gram Panchayat Office or Talati Chamber

steps.title: Submit Online Application on State e-District Portal
steps.description: Log into your state e-governance portal and choose Caste Certificate issuance service. Fill personal details, select your notified sub-caste name, and upload scanned proofs.
steps.calloutText: Select your sub-caste name exactly as spelled in the central or state gazette notification.

steps.title: Pay Nominal Statutory Application Fee
steps.description: Pay the statutory processing fee of twenty to fifty rupees online using UPI or Net Banking. Download and print the payment receipt containing the application tracking number.
steps.where: Online Payment Gateway or CSC Counter
steps.calloutText: Keep the application acknowledgement safe to track verification progress across revenue offices.

steps.title: Scrutiny and Field Inquiry by Social Welfare Committee
steps.description: The Revenue Inspector or Social Welfare Committee conducts field scrutiny of submitted school and land records. Once authenticity is verified, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate or Mamlatdar approves the file.

steps.title: Download Digitally Signed Caste Certificate
steps.description: Download your digitally signed Caste Certificate from the state portal or DigiLocker once approved. The digital certificate features an official QR code valid for all national admissions and government employment.
steps.calloutText: SC and ST caste certificates have lifetime legal validity and never expire.

documentRequirements.name: Father or Paternal Blood Relative Caste Certificate
documentRequirements.description: Certified copy of father, paternal uncle, or grandfather official caste certificate or school leaving certificate recording caste.

documentRequirements.name: Pre-Cutoff Domicile & Ancestral Residence Record
documentRequirements.description: Government revenue record, village birth entry, or school register establishing family stay in state prior to cut-off year.

documentRequirements.name: Applicant School Leaving Certificate
documentRequirements.description: Original or certified copy of school leaving certificate showing applicant date of birth, father name, and religion.

documentRequirements.name: Family Pedigree Chart (Vanshavali) with Talati Sign
documentRequirements.description: Family tree detailing paternal lineage from eldest recorded ancestor down to the applicant, signed by local Talati.

documentRequirements.name: Sworn Caste Self-Declaration Affidavit
documentRequirements.description: Affidavit executed on non-judicial stamp paper affirming caste category and declaring no false claims.

documentRequirements.name: Father Original State Caste Certificate for Migrants
documentRequirements.description: Official caste certificate issued by the original state government before migration to another territory.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Certified copy from original home state

documentRequirements.name: Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) Certificate for OBC Quota
documentRequirements.description: Official certificate confirming family annual income is below statutory creamy layer ceiling for OBC reservation.

rejectionReasons.title: Submitting Maternal Lineage Documents Instead of Paternal Proofs
rejectionReasons.description: Indian law strictly recognizes caste status derived from the biological father. Submitting maternal documents causes immediate rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Furnish caste or school leaving certificates of father, grandfather, or paternal uncles.

rejectionReasons.title: Inability to Provide Ancestral Residence Proofs Before Cut-Off Year
rejectionReasons.description: Failure to prove family residence in the state prior to 1950 for SC/ST or 1978 for OBC prevents eligibility verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Search old land revenue registers, municipal birth entries, or village school admission records.

rejectionReasons.title: Discrepancy Between Stated Sub-Caste and Notified Schedule
rejectionReasons.description: Colloquial clan names or slight spelling variations not found in the official presidential orders lead to document rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Select the exact recognized sub-caste name listed in the constitutional order schedule.

rejectionReasons.title: Submitting Unattested or Incomplete Family Pedigree Tree
rejectionReasons.description: Genealogy charts lacking official verification from the village Talati or Patwari are rejected during scrutiny.
rejectionReasons.solution: Have your complete paternal genealogy attested by your local Talati or village accountant.

rejectionReasons.title: Affidavit on Plain Paper Lacking Official Notary Seal
rejectionReasons.description: Caste declarations made on plain paper or without a registered notary stamp and registration number are invalid.
rejectionReasons.solution: Execute the affidavit on non-judicial stamp paper signed before an authorized notary.

rejectionReasons.title: Claiming State Benefits Without Origin State Caste Certification
rejectionReasons.description: Migrants who moved after the cut-off year cannot claim reservation in the new state without origin state verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for an on-migration certificate citing father origin state caste certificate.

faqItems.question: What is the legal basis of a Caste Certificate in India?
faqItems.answer: Caste certificates are issued under presidential orders and constitutional schedules to extend reservation and educational benefits.

faqItems.question: Can I claim my mother caste for reservation benefits?
faqItems.answer: Generally no. The Supreme Court has ruled that a child inherits the caste of the father under customary patrilineal law.

faqItems.question: What are statutory cut-off dates for caste certification?
faqItems.answer: Cut-off years require proving family residence before 1950 for SC/ST and 1978 for OBC in the specific state.

faqItems.question: Does a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe certificate expire?
faqItems.answer: No. SC and ST caste certificates have permanent lifetime validity and do not require periodic renewal.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between OBC certificate and Non-Creamy Layer certificate?
faqItems.answer: An OBC certificate confirms your community. A Non-Creamy Layer certificate confirms family income is below the reservation ceiling.

faqItems.question: Who is the competent issuing authority for caste certificates?
faqItems.answer: The Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Tehsildar, or Taluka Mamlatdar is the designated statutory issuing authority.

faqItems.question: Can I apply for a Caste Certificate online?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Most states offer online applications through their e-District portals or state citizen service platforms.

faqItems.question: Does a digitally signed caste certificate need a physical stamp?
faqItems.answer: No. Cryptographically signed certificates with verification QR codes are legally valid without physical ink stamps or signatures.

GJ.summary: Caste certificates in Gujarat for SC, ST, and SEBC are issued via Digital Gujarat by the Taluka Mamlatdar. A verified Vanshavali pedigree attested by the Talati and pre-1978 SEBC residency proof are compulsory prerequisites.
